quotes.text: The uncomfortable truth is this. Agentic isn't a UI choice. It's an operating model. A real agent behaves less like a chat widget and more like a distributed decision engine.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines an agentic workforce as an operating model rather than a chat interface.

quotes.text: Users will forgive, I don't know. They will not forgive, I'm sure, followed by being wrong.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures why confident wrong answers kill agent adoption and why grounding is mandatory.

quotes.text: SharePoint is not a knowledge strategy. It's a document landfill with a search box. And yes, Microsoft search has improved.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Provocative argument for building a curated, computable knowledge index for agents.

quotes.text: Prefer reusable tools over reusable agents agents are experiences tools are capabilities. When you standardize tools agents can stay small, domain scoped and disposable.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear design principle for scaling agents through standardized MCP tools.

quotes.text: The last transition is the simplest truth in the entire roadmap. Agents don't scale because they're intelligent. They scale because you made their decisions enforceable.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the episode's thesis that enforceability, not intelligence, makes agents scale.

The core misconception: automation is not an agentic workforce
IT ticket triage and Copilot Studio intent design

Confident wrong answers, grounding and Azure AI Search
MCP tools and three demo architectures
Agent sprawl, Entra Agent ID, governance and the day-by-day roadmap

takeaways: Start with one domain such as IT ticket triage, explicit KPIs like deflection and SLA reduction, and a containment boundary that defines what the agent must never do.
Enforce no source, no answer by grounding agents on a curated Azure AI Search index and exposing actions through a small set of governed MCP tools with read before write.
Give every agent an Entra Agent ID, an owner, gated publishing and approvals via Teams adaptive cards so the workforce scales without sprawl or ghost agents.
hook: Most Copilot and agent rollouts fail in week two when the first confident wrong answer reaches the wrong audience. This episode is for IT leaders and architects who need measurable results from Copilot Studio within 30 days. It lays out a roadmap from intent design and grounding to MCP tools and Entra Agent ID governance.
